correctness.rationale: At αA=cβ, x*=c/α=A/β, q=x/x*−1 leads exactly to q'=−βq−b(1+q)y, y'=cqy. The Lyapunov function V=x−x*−x*log(x/x*)+(b/α)y has V'=−β(x−x*)²/x and compact positive-state sublevels; the only invariant part of {V'=0} is (x*,0), giving global convergence for interior data. Defect r=q+(b/β)y solves r'=−βr+[b(c−β)/β]qy; variation of constants and y'/y→0 yield r/y→0, whence (1/y)'→bc/β and t y→β/(bc), t(x−x*)→−1/α. With a2=b²(β−c)/β³, second defect s=q+(b/β)y−a2y² obeys the exact stable equation printed in RESULT.md with cubic/quartic forcing; independently SymPy-simplified both sides and obtained zero residual. The bound s/y²→0 follows from stable variation of constants; then (1/y)'=bc/β−(c a2)y+o(y). As 1/y~(bc/β)t, integration yields logarithmic coefficient −(c a2)/(bc/β)=b(c−β)/β². All constants hold for any strictly positive initial x,y, not just near the fixed point; the y=0 invariant boundary is properly excluded.
